items.label: ARROW registry
items.summary: In 1,549 adolescents from the ARROW registry, average time to return-to-sport clearance rose from 8.6 months for surgeries in 2015 to 9.8 months in 2023, after accounting for age, sex, graft, and site.
facts: months longer for females than males

items.label: Psychological readiness
items.summary: In 58 patients about 6 months after ACL reconstruction, fear of movement, anxiety, and how patients rated their own knee explained readiness to return to sport far better than strength or hop symmetry did.

stat.caption: of the variation in readiness explained by the full model

facts: explained by knee-related quality of life

items.label: Physical activity
items.summary: Among 125 adolescents, the share who felt as active as before injury doubled from 6 to 9 months after surgery. Even so, half still felt less active or found activity harder at 9 months.

stat.caption: as active as before injury, 6 vs 9 months

facts: still less active or finding activity harder at 9 months

items.label: Reinjury risk
items.summary: In 579 patients followed for at least 2 years, 14% had a second ACL injury. A steeper quadriceps torque-velocity relationship and younger age both predicted who got hurt again.

stat.caption: had a second ACL injury (81 of 579)

facts: odds of reinjury with a steeper torque-velocity slope
lower odds for each year older
